query: Explain what leads a company to be based in one region rather than another.

per_column.name: industry_sector
per_column.rationale: Industry sector plausibly drives both where a company locates (sectors cluster geographically) and is a stable company attribute; a common cause candidate for regional location. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: tech_focus_area
per_column.rationale: The technology focus shapes location choice (e.g., AI/biotech hubs) and is an intrinsic firm characteristic, making it a plausible common driver of regional clustering. Surfaced from data, not the query.

per_column.name: company_stage
per_column.rationale: Firm maturity affects capacity/incentive to locate in expensive innovation hubs and is not on any mediating path forced by location; plausible common cause of location patterns. Not in query.

per_column.name: business_model_type
per_column.rationale: Business model (B2B software vs hardware vs consumer) plausibly influences where firms base and reflects firm type; a candidate common cause of regional choice.

per_column.name: deep_tech_rd_intensity
per_column.rationale: R&D intensity drives proximity to universities/talent hubs and is a firm attribute; plausible common driver of location. Not named in query.

per_column.name: physical_infrastructure_dependency
per_column.rationale: Dependence on manufacturing/data-center/lab infrastructure is a concrete candidate cause whose effect on where a company bases can be attributed -- functions as a treatment-like driver of location.

per_column.name: specialized_talent_signal
per_column.rationale: The type of specialized talent needed drives location toward talent pools and is a firm requirement; a plausible common cause of regional clustering.

judge.rationale: The added columns are all firm-attribute drivers of location, and none were named in the highly generic query, so they were genuinely surfaced from the data. However, the design does NOT cleanly realise a causal-attribution setup: there is no single, well-delineated TREATMENT distinguished from CONFOUNDERS. All columns are alternative candidate causes of the outcome sitting at the same level, functioning more as a multi-factor explanatory regression than a treatment-plus-adjustment-set. Because a confounder must be a common cause of BOTH a treatment and the outcome, and no treatment is privileged, these variables cannot be verified as genuine confounders rather than parallel treatments -- they are just co-drivers. Talent needs and infrastructure dependency are also plausibly mediators of industry/tech-focus effects on location, blurring roles. The set is sensible for explanation but weak as a rigorous causal estimation scaffold, hence low confounder_quality.
